answer: A concrete Sybil defense is the slashable identity bond. Before an agent may vote or claim work, it must lock collateral in a public registry. To mint N fake peers, an attacker has to post N separate bonds, so his capital cost grows linearly with every clone, and one caught duplicate triggers slashing that burns the entire stake. In a bazaar trading velvet and walnut, a cheating bot cannot simply wander in under a hundred fresh names without risking a hundred deposits. Identities stay easy to read but expensive to counterfeit.
